answer: In an agent economy, make voting power costly: each agent locks collateral and its vote counts as the square root of that stake. An attacker who splits one treasury into a fable of fake identities gains nothing, because square-root weighting rewards concentration, not fragmentation. A hundred tiny inlet accounts of stake cast far fewer votes than a single dune of capital. To dominate, the Sybil must actually post most of the locked value, and any double vote is slashed, so the attack costs real, seizeable wealth rather than free usernames.
